title: Servvia access-token claims
description: Decoded payload of every JWT access token the Servvia API issues and accepts as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (Passport strategy `jwt`). All five kinds are signed with ONE shared HMAC secret (env var JWT_ACCESS_SECRET), algorithm HS256, JWS header {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}. There is no `iss`, `aud`, `jti` or `nbf` claim; `iat` and `exp` (NumericDate seconds) are added by @nestjs/jwt / jsonwebtoken at signing time. COEXISTENCE RULE: while the Go service and the NestJS API run side by side, Go must verify exactly these tokens with the same JWT_ACCESS_SECRET value and HS256, accept every branch below with identical semantics (including the absent-`kind` staff token), and, if Go ever mints tokens, emit byte-compatible claims so NestJS accepts them. The refresh token is a separate JWT with a separate secret, documented in $defs.refreshToken; it is never accepted as an access token. Nest-side acceptance check (JwtStrategy.validate) only requires `sub`, `role` and `organizationId` to be truthy; `kind` is not validated against the enum at verification time.

x-verification.tokenLocation: Authorization header, scheme `Bearer` (ExtractJwt.fromAuthHeaderAsBearerToken). WebSocket handshake additionally accepts socket.io `handshake.auth.token`.
x-verification.failureResponse: HTTP 401 {"statusCode":401,"message":"Unauthorized"} for missing/invalid/expired signature; HTTP 401 {"message":"Malformed token payload","error":"Unauthorized","statusCode":401} when sub/role/organizationId is missing.
x-verification.startupGuard: Production boot refuses the checked-in example values of JWT_ACCESS_SECRET / JWT_REFRESH_SECRET.

x-expiry-format: Expiry env values are passed to jsonwebtoken `expiresIn`. A string is parsed with the `ms` library ('15m', '12h', '30d'); a number is seconds. Note: a bare numeric STRING such as '900' is parsed by `ms` as milliseconds.
x-known-issues: The WebSocket gateway verifies tokens via AuthService.verifyAccessToken, which does NOT pin `algorithms` (jsonwebtoken then allows HS256/HS384/HS512 for a string secret), unlike JwtStrategy which pins HS256. Source: apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts:155

Story 2.5: every token whose subject is a staff member (staff session, tablet_staff, tablet_manager) is re-checked on use, in Nest (JwtStrategy) and Go (identity.RequireActiveStaff and realtime): the Staff row must be active, not deleted, in an active organization, and a staff session's `sid` must not be revoked (Redis key `auth:revoked-session:<sid>`, written on logout). A check that cannot be made fails closed. Tablet kinds are additionally revoked with their device on routes that add TabletDeviceGuard/TabletTokenActiveGuard.

`kind: 'staff'` is declared in the TypeScript union but no code path ever issues it; staff tokens omit `kind`. Both forms are treated as a staff session by StaffSessionOnlyGuard and resolveVenueScope. Source: apps/api/src/auth/interfaces/jwt-payload.interface.ts:22
Device token `email` claims use the literal domain `@verdura.internal` (a real value, not a mailbox). Source: apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts:137, apps/api/src/tablet/tablet-auth.service.ts:129

A kind value outside the enum (only mintable with the secret) would be treated as unrestricted staff by resolveVenueScope but rejected by StaffSessionOnlyGuard. Source: apps/api/src/auth/utils/resolve-venue-scope.ts:30, apps/api/src/auth/guards/staff-session-only.guard.ts:21

uuid.description: Prisma `@default(uuid())` identifier (Staff.id, Venue.id, Organization.id, TabletDevice.id). Source: apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:282, apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:380

staffRole.description: Prisma enum StaffRole. `owner` bypasses every @Roles check in RolesGuard. Source: apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:10, apps/api/src/auth/guards/roles.guard.ts:42

numericDate.description: Seconds since Unix epoch, added by jsonwebtoken.

staffAccessToken.title: Staff access token (Admin Console login session)
staffAccessToken.description: Issued by POST /api/auth/login, POST /api/auth/admin-pin and POST /api/auth/refresh. Organization-wide: no venueId, so resolveVenueScope does not restrict it. `kind` is absent in every issued token. `sid` names the login session shared with its refresh token; a staff session without `sid` is refused (Story 2.5).

sid.description: Login session ID, created at login and kept on refresh. Logout revokes it for every token of the session.

kind.description: Never issued; accepted and treated as a staff session if present.

kdsDeviceToken.title: KDS device token (kitchen display terminal)
kdsDeviceToken.description: Issued by POST /api/kiosk/kds/auth after a venue PIN check. Pinned to one venue. `sub` is synthetic, not a Staff row. No deviceId.

tabletDeviceToken.title: Order Tablet device token (restricted/customer context)
tabletDeviceToken.description: Issued by POST /api/tablet/enroll. Pinned to the device's venue. `sub` is synthetic. Carries deviceId so TabletDeviceGuard / TabletTokenActiveGuard can check live TabletDevice.status.
x-known-issues: No endpoint renews a tablet_device token; once `exp` passes the device must be re-enrolled with a new bootstrap token. The durable device secret generated at enrollment is hashed and stored but never returned, so it cannot be used for renewal. Source: apps/api/src/tablet/tablet-auth.service.ts:306

tabletStaffToken.title: Order Tablet named-staff elevation token
tabletStaffToken.description: Issued by POST /api/tablet/elevate. Identity is the real Staff row (sub = Staff.id, role = Staff.role) but still pinned to the device's venue and device.

sub.description: Staff.id of the elevated staff member.

role.description: Staff.role at elevation time (any role; not re-checked against the token later except by TabletStaffGuard, which only checks active/not deleted).

venueId.description: Copied from the calling device token, not from the staff record.

tabletManagerToken.title: Order Tablet manager step-up token
tabletManagerToken.description: Issued by POST /api/tablet/manager-step-up. sub = manager Staff.id; role is one of manager/admin/owner at issue time. `actingStaffId` is present only when the caller's token was kind `tablet_staff` (it is that token's `sub`); otherwise the key is omitted (undefined is dropped by JSON serialisation).

actingStaffId.description: Staff.id of the tablet_staff session that requested step-up.

refreshToken.title: Staff refresh token (cookie)
refreshToken.description: Separate JWT carried only in the `refresh_token` cookie and accepted only by Passport strategy `jwt-refresh` on POST /api/auth/refresh. Signed HS256 with JWT_REFRESH_SECRET (distinct from JWT_ACCESS_SECRET). Custom claims are `sub` and `sid` (the login session). Not rotated on refresh. Revocable: logout writes the Redis key `auth:revoked-session:<sid>` for the refresh token's remaining lifetime (Story 2.5). On use, sub must be a UUID of an existing Staff row with isActive=true and `sid` must be present and not revoked, else 401 'Session expired or account deactivated'; a revocation check that cannot be made fails closed (500).

x-cookie.name: refresh_token
x-cookie.path: /api/auth (Story 2.5; was /api/auth/refresh, which kept the cookie from POST /api/auth/logout)
x-cookie.maxAgeMs: ms(JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRY), default ms('7d') = 604800000 (Express also emits the matching Expires attribute)

x-known-issues: Refresh does not rotate the refresh token; a copied refresh token remains valid until exp, logout or deactivation. Source: apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts
Revocations live in Redis. A Redis data loss forgets logouts (not deactivations, which are read from PostgreSQL) until the tokens expire; Redis persistence in production is not verified.

sid.description: Login session ID, shared with the session's access tokens.
